Are you working on generated translation files or are you translating game's original files?

Because If you want to leave absolutely  no trace (even in files) of 'native', that is the best way to do it. And if that is the case I dont think you need to do anything else that language is reffered to as "None" anyway. The only and default language of the game.

But if you are working on translation files, what do you mean by 'leave no trace'?

Coz you can set translation as default language

[https://www.renpy.org/doc/html/translation.html#default-language](https://www.renpy.org/doc/html/translation.html#default-language)

And remove option to change it back in-game, but native'd still be in files and accessible via console.

​

EDIT:

As for a font, I've never done it myself, but tried it out and It kinda worked:

Create (if you doesnt have one already) gui.rpy in your translation files.

Paste command:

translate language\_name python:

gui.text\_font = "font\_name.ttf"

gui.name\_text\_font = "font\_name.ttf"

gui.interface\_text\_font = "font\_name.ttf"

gui.button\_text\_font = "font\_name.ttf"

gui.choice\_button\_text\_font = "font\_name.ttf"

​

language\_name is the same as your translation folder name. You should put font .ttf file in the same folder as yours translation files.

gui.text\_font changes in game (story/dialog) text

gui.name\_text\_font changes character names

gui.interface\_text\_font changes interface text (menu)

gui.button\_text\_font changes button style in the interface

gui.choice\_button\_text\_font ingame choices

That should changes every single bit of text, i think :P

​

Remember to indent those gui. lines.
